ui-size-reverse: Maps the smallest values to the maximum size and the largest values to the minimum size. Works with proportional and percentile scales. Equal values keep equal sizes; a constant series keeps the minimum size.
ui-layout-score-reverse: Reverses concentric ring order: lower degree, metric or attribute values occupy inner rings. Equal scores still share a ring. Apply the layout to update positions.
_instructions: Tooltip text is stored here. UI elements reference entries by data-tooltip key; edit the text value to change a tooltip.

tooltips.path-enlarge-nodes: Optionally scale highlighted path nodes relative to their current sizes. Off by default, preserving the original sizes. This changes only the display, not the graph attributes.
tooltips.path-edge-scale: Scale highlighted path edge thickness relative to each edge's current displayed thickness. 1 preserves original widths. Shared edges are scaled once, and stored graph weights are not changed.
tooltips.path-specific-edge-color: Choose this path's edge color. On shared edges, the most recently highlighted or recolored path takes precedence. Colors are remembered when paths are de-highlighted or the color mode is changed.
tooltips.node-label-attribute: Choose the attribute displayed as the node label. Missing or empty values fall back to the node ID.
tooltips.edge-label-attribute: Choose the attribute displayed as the edge label. Missing or empty values have no label. Enable Show edge labels to display them.
tooltips.path-edge-highlight: Default preserves original edge colors. Single color uses one color for all highlighted path edges and arrows. Color for each path uses the color pickers in the path table. Node colors and edge thickness are independent of this setting.
tooltips.ui-multi-node-select: Turn on multi-selection to add nodes by clicking them, or use Select area to draw a rectangle. Drag any selected node to move the selected group together. Requires Drag nodes.
tooltips.ui-area-select-nodes: Draw a rectangle in the graph to select the nodes inside it. Hold Shift, Ctrl, or Command while drawing to add them to the current multi-selection.
tooltips.ui-geographic-projection: Web Mercator uses OpenStreetMap street tiles. Equal Earth preserves relative areas on a spherical world map with Natural Earth land and country boundaries, including the poles. Background and nodes use the same projection.
tooltips.ui-geographic-latitude: Numeric node attribute containing latitude in decimal degrees. Every node needs a finite value: ±85.05112878° for Mercator, or ±90° for Equal Earth. Computed metrics are not coordinates.
tooltips.ui-geographic-longitude: Numeric node attribute containing longitude in decimal degrees, from −180° to 180°. Date-line wrapping is selected automatically to keep nearby geographic nodes together.
tooltips.ui-layout-distance-length: Desired geometric length for one shortest-path distance unit. Stress majorization targets this scale times the graph distance.
tooltips.ui-layout-kk-size: Kamada–Kawai's drawing size L0. Desired spring lengths are L0 times graph distance divided by the component's graph diameter.
tooltips.ui-layout-spring-constant: Kamada–Kawai's K: spring stiffness is K divided by squared graph distance. This changes gradient magnitude and the meaning of tolerance.
tooltips.ui-layout-distance-weighted: Interpret positive edge weights as shortest-path lengths. Off uses hop counts. Directions are ignored; the shortest reciprocal or parallel edge is used.
tooltips.ui-layout-stress-tolerance: Stop when relative stress reduction per majorization step is at most this value. Stress is the sum of squared relative errors against target graph distances.
tooltips.ui-layout-kk-tolerance: Stop when every movable node's spring-energy gradient magnitude is at most this value. Each animation step performs one Newton update of the selected node.
tooltips.ui-layout-hu-tolerance: Stop a level when the Euclidean norm of all node movements in a sweep is below tolerance times that level's nominal edge length K.
tooltips.ui-layout-hu-scale: Scale of the seeded initial drawing. Coarsest K is derived from its average edge length; scale is the fallback for an edgeless or coincident drawing.
tooltips.ui-layout-hu-repulsion: Hu's C. Repulsive force magnitude is C times K squared divided by distance. The paper uses C = 0.2.
tooltips.ui-layout-hu-cooling: Hu's t in (0,1). Fine levels multiply step length by t each sweep. Coarsest adaptive cooling shrinks on increased force energy and grows after five successive decreases.
tooltips.ui-layout-hu-level-iterations: Maximum sweeps at each hierarchy level. Reaching it advances to the next finer level and reports limit reached. The common iteration budget also applies across all levels.
tooltips.ui-layout-hu-weighted: Use positive edge weights as attraction strengths. Off uses unit original edges. Coarse weights always sum the strengths of crossing edges.
tooltips.ui-layout-community-inner: Published model used independently within each supplied community, with its default hyperparameters. Community detection is not performed by this layout.
tooltips.ui-layout-community-outer: Published model for the quotient graph whose nodes are communities. Hu uses crossing-edge counts as attraction strengths; distance models use unweighted community hops.
tooltips.ui-layout-community-gap: Minimum separation between circular envelopes around communities after quotient layout. Conflicting pinned envelopes cannot be separated.
tooltips.ui-layout-community-iterations: Iteration budget independently applied to each community layout and the quotient layout. Returned diagnostics sum their completed iterations.
tooltips.ui-btn-session: Save or open a RELISON session (.relison)
tooltips.ui-inspector-toggle: Show or hide the selection inspector
tooltips.ui-focus-toggle: Reduce visual clutter while keeping every control available
tooltips.ui-circlepack-group-field: Choose a community assignment or node attribute to group nodes. Groups define rings, columns or clusters, depending on the layout. Bipartite and multipartite groups must obey their edge constraints.
tooltips.ui-circlepack-group: Choose a community assignment or node attribute to group nodes. Groups define rings, columns or clusters, depending on the layout. Bipartite and multipartite groups must obey their edge constraints.
tooltips.ui-layout-radius-field: Radius of the circular layout in coordinate units. Increasing it spreads nodes farther from the centre.
tooltips.ui-layout-radius: Radius of the circular layout in coordinate units. Increasing it spreads nodes farther from the centre.
tooltips.ui-layout-spacing-field: Separation in coordinate units: grid cell spacing, distance between rings, or vertical spacing within columns. For trees, sibling separation; for Sugiyama, minimum horizontal centre separation, including edge bend points.
tooltips.ui-layout-spacing: Separation in coordinate units: grid cell spacing, distance between rings, or vertical spacing within columns. For trees, sibling separation; for Sugiyama, minimum horizontal centre separation, including edge bend points.
tooltips.ui-layout-root-field: Starting node for ego layouts or preferred root for a tree. Leave empty to choose automatically. Directed tree roots must have no parent.
tooltips.ui-layout-root: Starting node for ego layouts or preferred root for a tree. Leave empty to choose automatically. Directed tree roots must have no parent.
tooltips.ui-layout-direction-field: Outgoing follows source to target; incoming reverses edges; ignore direction follows either way; mutual follows only connections present in both directions.
tooltips.ui-layout-direction: Outgoing follows source to target; incoming reverses edges; ignore direction follows either way; mutual follows only connections present in both directions.
tooltips.ui-layout-column-spacing-field: Horizontal distance between feature, partition or hop-distance columns, in coordinate units.
tooltips.ui-layout-column-spacing: Horizontal distance between feature, partition or hop-distance columns, in coordinate units.
tooltips.ui-layout-level-spacing-field: Vertical distance between successive tree depths or Sugiyama layers, in coordinate units.
tooltips.ui-layout-level-spacing: Vertical distance between successive tree depths or Sugiyama layers, in coordinate units.
tooltips.ui-layout-sweeps-field: Number of downward/upward ordering passes. More passes take longer. Sugiyama keeps the best crossing count seen and also performs coordinate sweeps. Zero preserves initial within-column or within-layer order.
tooltips.ui-layout-sweeps: Number of downward/upward ordering passes. More passes take longer. Sugiyama keeps the best crossing count seen and also performs coordinate sweeps. Zero preserves initial within-column or within-layer order.
tooltips.ui-layout-columns-field: Number of grid columns. Zero chooses approximately the square root of the node count; the final row may be incomplete.
tooltips.ui-layout-columns: Number of grid columns. Zero chooses approximately the square root of the node count; the final row may be incomplete.
tooltips.ui-layout-width-field: Width of the random initialization rectangle, centred on the origin, in coordinate units.
tooltips.ui-layout-width: Width of the random initialization rectangle, centred on the origin, in coordinate units.
tooltips.ui-layout-height-field: Height of the random initialization rectangle, centred on the origin, in coordinate units.
tooltips.ui-layout-height: Height of the random initialization rectangle, centred on the origin, in coordinate units.
tooltips.ui-layout-seed-field: Seed for random positions. The same graph order, seed and settings reproduce initialization. With a warm start, only nodes without supplied positions use random initialization.
tooltips.ui-layout-seed: Seed for random positions. The same graph order, seed and settings reproduce initialization. With a warm start, only nodes without supplied positions use random initialization.
tooltips.ui-layout-iterations: Maximum force iterations for this run, up to 5000. The layout may converge sooner. Zero shows initialization only. There is no computation time limit.
tooltips.ui-layout-theta: Barnes–Hut approximation threshold for repulsion. Zero evaluates exact node pairs. Larger values usually run faster but approximate forces less accurately.
tooltips.ui-layout-tolerance: Maximum node movement per iteration, in coordinate units, used to detect convergence. The layout stops after five consecutive iterations at or below this value. Larger values accept less refinement.
tooltips.ui-layout-warm-start: Start from the currently displayed coordinates instead of new seeded random positions. Useful for continuing or refining an existing arrangement.
tooltips.ui-layout-remove-overlap: Separate circular node glyphs after the force session finishes. Uses the radius and gap below; may change the final force geometry.
tooltips.ui-layout-node-radius: Radius assumed for every node during overlap removal or ForceAtlas2 collision forces, in layout coordinate units. This is independent of rendered pixel size.
tooltips.ui-layout-overlap-gap: Minimum extra distance between node glyph boundaries during overlap removal, in coordinate units.
tooltips.ui-layout-fr-bounded: Derive the edge scale from the frame area, clamp positions to its borders, and cool linearly over the iteration budget.
tooltips.ui-layout-fr-width: Width of the centred FR drawing frame in layout coordinate units.
tooltips.ui-layout-fr-height: Height of the centred FR drawing frame in layout coordinate units.
tooltips.ui-layout-fr-temperature: Maximum initial movement per iteration. Decreases linearly to zero in reference mode.
tooltips.ui-layout-ideal-length: Characteristic edge-length scale for Fruchterman–Reingold. Larger values favour a more spread-out drawing. Also sets the initial maximum movement per iteration; edge lengths are not guaranteed to equal it.
tooltips.ui-layout-cooling: Multiplier applied to the maximum movement after each Fruchterman–Reingold iteration. A lower value freezes movement sooner; a value closer to one allows longer refinement.
tooltips.ui-layout-weighted: Multiply Fruchterman–Reingold attraction by edge weight. Larger weights pull endpoints together more strongly. Used weights must be finite and non-negative.
tooltips.ui-layout-fa-scaling: ForceAtlas2 repulsion strength. Increasing it generally spreads nodes farther apart relative to edge attraction.
tooltips.ui-layout-fa-gravity: ForceAtlas2 attraction toward the coordinate origin. Higher values keep the drawing more compact; zero disables gravity.
tooltips.ui-layout-jitter: Tolerance used by ForceAtlas2 adaptive speed control. Higher values allow faster movement but can increase oscillation.
tooltips.ui-layout-weight-influence: Exponent applied to edge weights in ForceAtlas2 attraction. Zero ignores weights; one uses them directly. Larger exponents emphasize differences. Used weights must be finite and non-negative.
tooltips.ui-layout-linlog: Use logarithmic rather than linear attraction in ForceAtlas2. Long edges pull less strongly, which can emphasize separation between groups.
tooltips.ui-layout-strong-gravity: Make ForceAtlas2 gravity grow with distance from the origin rather than have constant magnitude for a given node mass. Helps restrain distant nodes.
tooltips.ui-layout-outbound: Divide edge attraction by source degree mass and compensate by mean node mass. Edge direction determines the source.
tooltips.ui-layout-adjust-sizes: Use overlap radius in ForceAtlas2 forces. Uses exact repulsion and the reference collision-mode movement limiter.
tooltips.ui-layout-normalize-weights: Rescale weights to zero through one before applying weight influence. Equal weights become one.
tooltips.ui-layout-invert-weights: Replace nonzero weights by their reciprocal before normalization and weight influence. Zero stays zero.
tooltips.ui-layout-score-field: Score used to assign concentric rings. Equal scores share a ring; higher scores go nearer the centre. Choose degree, a computed metric or a numeric node attribute.
tooltips.ui-layout-score: Score used to assign concentric rings. Equal scores share a ring; higher scores go nearer the centre. Choose degree, a computed metric or a numeric node attribute.
tooltips.ui-layout-preset-x-field: Source for horizontal coordinates: saved positions or a numeric node attribute. Attribute values retain their original units and must be finite for every node.
tooltips.ui-layout-preset-x: Source for horizontal coordinates: saved positions or a numeric node attribute. Attribute values retain their original units and must be finite for every node.
tooltips.ui-layout-preset-y-field: Source for vertical coordinates: saved positions or a numeric node attribute. Attribute values retain their original units and must be finite for every node.
tooltips.ui-layout-preset-y: Source for vertical coordinates: saved positions or a numeric node attribute. Attribute values retain their original units and must be finite for every node.
tooltips.ui-layout-pack-components: Arrange disconnected components separately after layout, preserving each component shape. This can shift columns or coordinate axes. Components containing pinned nodes stay fixed.
tooltips.ui-layout-packing-gap: Padding used when packing component bounding boxes, in coordinate units. Boxes are based on node centres, not rendered glyph sizes.

tooltips.ui-btn-export-edges: Export the edges table as CSV

tooltips.ui-btn-rec-eval-export: Export the evaluation table as CSV
tooltips.ui-diff-run-label: Optional name for this run in the metric plots; leave blank for an automatic label
tooltips.ui-btn-diff-gif: Download the animation as a GIF
tooltips.ui-btn-diff-webm: Download the animation as a WebM video
tooltips.ui-btn-diff-upload-menu: Upload information pieces or their features
tooltips.ui-btn-diff-piece-download: Download the information pieces as TSV
tooltips.ui-btn-diff-feature-add: Add a feature column to the table
tooltips.ui-diff-feature-view: Feature shown on the piece chips and distribution bars
tooltips.js-recommendation-multigraph: Recommendation is not available for multigraphs.
tooltips.js-add-link: Add this link to the graph
tooltips.js-metric-needs-feature: Needs a feature attribute to be meaningful.
tooltips.js-add-information-piece-to-run: Add at least one information piece (in the "Information pieces" subtab) to run.
